title: Diversification practices reduce organic to conventional yield gap
publisher: Proceedings of the Royal Society B
methodology: Meta-analysis related to diversification and organic versus conventional systems.
limitations: Yield-gap focus; pollinator benefits are mechanistic inferences supported by related diversification literature, not a farm-specific census.

chunks.text: Diversification practices such as multi-cropping and habitat heterogeneity are associated with ecological benefits in farming systems, including resources for pollinators and other beneficial invertebrates. Simplified pesticide-intensive monocultures reduce floral and nesting resources. The evidence supports habitat and cropping diversification as a biodiversity intervention, not a precise local abundance forecast.
